pairs: Quis credidit auditui nostro?
Who has believed our report?
et brachium Domini cui revelatum est?
And to whom has the arm of the Lord been revealed?
Et ascendet sicut virgultum coram eo,
And he will rise up like a tender plant in his sight,
et sicut radix de terra sitienti.
and like a root from the thirsty ground.
Non est species ei,
There is no beautiful
neque decor,
or stately appearance in him.
et vidimus eum,
For we looked upon him,
et non erat aspectus,
and there was no aspect,
et desideravimus eum:
such that we would desire him.
despectum, et novissimum virorum,
He is despised and the least among men,
virum dolorum, et scientem infirmitatem,
a man of sorrows who knows infirmity.
et quasi absconditus vultus ejus et despectus,
And his countenance was hidden and despised. Because of this,
unde nec reputavimus eum.
we did not esteem him.
Vere languores nostros ipse tulit,
Truly,
et dolores nostros ipse portavit;
he has taken away our weaknesses,
et nos putavimus eum quasi leprosum,
and he himself has carried our sorrows.
et percussum a Deo,
And we thought of him as if he were a leper,
et humiliatum.
or as if he had been struck by God and humiliated.
Ipse autem vulneratus est propter iniquitates nostras;
But he himself was wounded because of our iniquities.
attritus est propter scelera nostra:
He was bruised because of our wickedness.
disciplina pacis nostræ super eum,
The discipline of our peace was upon him.
et livore ejus sanati sumus.
And by his wounds, we are healed.
Omnes nos quasi oves erravimus,
We have all gone astray like sheep;
unusquisque in viam suam declinavit:
each one has turned aside to his own way.
et posuit Dominus in eo iniquitatem omnium nostrum.
And the Lord has placed all our iniquity upon him.
Oblatus est quia ipse voluit,
He was offered up, because it was his own will.
et non aperuit os suum;
And he did not open his mouth.
sicut ovis ad occisionem ducetur,
He will be led like a sheep to the slaughter.
et quasi agnus coram tondente se obmutescet,
And he will be mute like a lamb before his shearer.
et non aperiet os suum.
For he will not open his mouth.
De angustia,
He was lifted up from anguish and judgment.
et de judicio sublatus est.
Who will describe his life?
Generationem ejus quis enarrabit?
For he has been cut off from the land of the living.
quia abscissus est de terra viventium:
Because of the wickedness of my people,
propter scelus populi mei percussi eum.
I have struck him down.
Et dabit impios pro sepultura,
And he will be given a place with the impious for his burial,
et divitem pro morte sua,
and with the rich for his death,
eo quod iniquitatem non fecerit,
though he has done no iniquity,
neque dolus fuerit in ore ejus.
nor was deceit in his mouth.
Et Dominus voluit conterere eum in infirmitate.
But it was the will of the Lord to crush him with infirmity.
Si posuerit pro peccato animam suam,
If he lays down his life because of sin,
videbit semen longævum,
he will see offspring with long lives,
et voluntas Domini in manu ejus dirigetur.
and the will of the Lord will be directed by his hand.
Pro eo quod laboravit anima ejus,
Because his soul has labored,
videbit
he will see and be satisfied.
et saturabitur.
By his knowledge,
In scientia sua justificabit ipse justus servus meus multos,
my just servant will himself justify many,
et iniquitates eorum ipse portabit.
and he himself will carry their iniquities.
Ideo dispertiam ei plurimos,
Therefore, I will allot to him a great number.
et fortium dividet spolia, pro eo quod tradidit in mortem animam suam,
And he will divide the spoils of the strong. For he has handed over his life to death,
et cum sceleratis reputatus est,
and he was reputed among criminals.
et ipse peccata multorum tulit,
And he has taken away the sins of many,
et pro transgressoribus rogavit.
and he has prayed for the transgressors.
